newsitem.title: USA: FAA proposes corrosion inspection for Boeings.
newsitem.headline: FAA proposes corrosion inspection for Boeings.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration said on Monday it proposed inspections of some 650 Boeing Co 747s for possible corrosion and cracking of an upper deck floor beam.
It said there had been no breaks in the beam, but if one did break it could result in extensive damage to other parts of the deck and possible rapid decompression of the airplane.

The FAA said that in 1990 some corrosion was found where a stainless steel threshold at the cart lift cutout in the upper deck was joined to the aluminum floor structure, and a new panel was ordered to be fitted.
But there may have been a manufacturing defect in the new panel and a corrosion and cracking inspection was now needed.
The FAA said that of about 650 Boeing 747s involved, some 180 are in the fleets of U.S. carriers.
